evidence.requirements: Most of the brief is met. Start page: heading, 25 exact-name links, family, L3, Search with alternative names and space-insensitive matching (format.js:62-71), Family select, "<n> cartridges" (list.jpg). Detail view: facts, capacity with source link, tables grouped Cartridge/Chamber with Symbol/Value/Unit, tolerance shown inline ("39.62 -0.2"), Print button, All cartridges link, hash route that survives reload (app.js:106-114). Drawing: inline SVG at 1 unit = 1 mm, hatched section, centre line, title block, a missing-value note (app.js:93-95). Unmet or partly met: (1) Print: the drawing is not at full width. style.css:108 fixes it to 115mm high, so it fills about half the A4 width (print-308_win.jpg). The title block text in print is huge and garbled, so the rule "every label legible" fails. (2) Diameter dimensions (P1, P2, H1, H2, G1, E1) are drawn across the part with long leaders and no extension lines (drawing.js:290-298). Only the lengths and R1 have extension lines. (3) Rule 8: on belted cases w also takes E + tb, because the groove branch runs as well (drawing.js:201-202), where the brief says to use the ramp end + tb. (4) None of the process artefacts asked for were delivered: no README, specs, ADRs or CI.
evidence.correctness: Most geometry follows the rules. Rim type comes from R1/P1 (drawing.js:18-22). The chamfer uses min(f·tanβ, R1/4) (:150). Groove floor and ramp are drawn, and on belted cases the ramp runs at δ to R3, then to E, then steps to P1 (:157-161; the belt shows in detail-300_win_mag.jpg). The rimfire half-round has ρ = min(R/2, (R1-P1)/2) (:140). Shoulder corners are rounded with r1 min and r2 (:174-185). The tangent ogive is mathematically correct, with its centre on the radial line and ending at m/2. Seating and k fractions match the brief per shape and category (:220-222). The heeled bullet uses H2 and H2-2tb (:227). Pocket sizes and depths are correct (:24-29). Labels match the data: 'L3 51.18', 'α 40°', 'α 10°58'0"'. Proportions match reference/308_win.png and reference/300_win_mag.png. Defects: (a) In print, the CSS rule `.drawing text { font-size: inherit; }` (style.css:113) overrides the title block's font-size attributes. The title block text then inherits 9pt (about 12 user units), overflows its box and overprints itself (print-308_win.jpg). (b) Straight cases use tb up to the mouth (wallAt, drawing.js:195), but the section bullet keeps G1/2. On 9 mm Luger and 44 Rem. Mag. the seated bullet overlaps the case wall by about 0.3 mm. (c) The belted w deviates from the rule, as noted under requirements. The printed page does fit one A4 page.
evidence.security: All data goes through esc() before innerHTML (app.js:8-10, 44-46, 53-54, 66, 76) and SVG text goes through esc (drawing.js:413). There is no eval or Function in app code; w.eval appears only in the jsdom test harness. No fonts, CDNs or fetch. The capacity URL is escaped, and it is followed only when the user clicks it.
evidence.code_quality: Small, readable split: data.js, format.js (display rules), drawing.js (model, then SVG), app.js (routing and rendering). Helpers have clear names (rimTypeOf, pocketOf, roundCorner, noseSamples, placeLabels). Weaknesses: buildDrawing is one function of about 270 lines (drawing.js:115-384). Scripts mix var and const and share globals. Bullet parameters are chained ternaries (:220-222). The title block depends on a CSS/attribute interplay that breaks in print. The unknown key case is handled ('Cartridge not found').
evidence.tests: Three node:test suites. format.test.js covers symbols, angles, units, inline tolerance, grouping, search ('7,62 x 51', '22lr') and the family counts. drawing.test.js covers rim types, wall and pocket values, groove points, the belt ramp at δ, the rimfire half-round, the heeled heel diameter, the ogive circle test, seating depths, missing-value reporting, and a label-overlap check over all 25 records. app.test.js uses jsdom to cover the list, search, filter, detail facts and tables, print click and hash routing. Gaps: nothing exercises print CSS (the garbled title block slipped through), shoulder geometry and the α arc, flat and semi-wadcutter noses, belted w, or bullet/wall clearance on straight cases.
evidence.ux_design: The tables are dense, right-aligned and use tabular numbers. The facts block is compact. Drawing labels do not overlap (detail-308_win.jpg). However, the drawing labels are fixed at 3.2 mm in the scaled SVG, so they render about twice the size of the page heading. The title block has a heavy, scaled border (style.css:81 lacks non-scaling-stroke) and is larger than the drawing on short cases (detail-9_mm_luger.jpg, detail-22_long_rifle.jpg). Staggered callouts leave a tall empty band above the drawing. Print: the drawing is about half width and the title block is unreadable overprinted text (print-308_win.jpg). In print, table header cells are larger than the data rows (th 0.85rem against 7pt). Dark mode exists in CSS but was not captured.
evidence.accessibility: The SVG has role=img and aria-label "<name> drawing" (drawing.js:421). Inputs are wrapped in label elements (Search, Family), the count uses aria-live='polite' (app.js:24), tables have th headers, facts use dl, headings run h1/h2/h3, and lang='en' is set. Everything uses native controls, so it works by keyboard with default focus rings. Muted text #5d6671 on white passes AA. Minor gaps: no scope or caption on tables, and the drawing has no longer description beyond its name (the tables do carry the data).
evidence.simplicity: Plain HTML, CSS and JS with no build step. The only dev dependency is jsdom. Roughly 430 lines for the drawing and about 120 for the app, which fits the problem. No needless abstractions.
evidence.maintainability: There is no README, no docs, no specs, no ADRs and no CI configuration. package.json has only `node --test`, jsdom is a caret range (^25.0.1), and there is no engines field or .nvmrc for Node 22. A package-lock is present. The version is a bare 1.0.0 with no release notes. The tests are a decent regression net, and the code comments explain the coordinate conventions (drawing.js:1-3). A newcomer would have to reverse-engineer the drawing rules from the brief.
evidence.visual_design: Tables and the list are calm and consistent (list.jpg). The drawing clashes with the rest of the page: drawing text is far larger than body text, and the title block has a thick black border several pixels wide that dominates every detail page (detail-22_long_rifle.jpg, detail-44_rem_mag.jpg). Line weights in the drawing are fine, and the hatching and dash-dot centre line read well. The print output looks broken.
evidence.layout: Hierarchy is sound: name, facts, drawing, then two-column table groups (detail-308_win.jpg). Space is wasted by the oversized title block and the tall label stack above the drawing. On short cartridges the title block is wider and taller than the cartridge itself. The Print and All cartridges links come before the heading. Print fits one page, but the drawing is not full width and the title block overflows its frame.
evidence.usability: Finding a cartridge is quick: live search across alternative names with spaces ignored, a family filter that combines with search, and a live count. Each name links to a bookmarkable hash URL. The detail view has Print and All cartridges, and an unknown key shows a clear not-found message. The 'Not drawn, not published: α, L1, L2…' note on straight cases is noise for those users.
evidence.reception: Reloaders and engineers would trust the data tables and the true-to-scale geometry. The cartoonishly large labels and title block look unfinished, and the garbled printed title block would hurt credibility the first time someone prints a sheet, which is a core task for this audience.

unmet_requirements: Printed detail view: the drawing is not at full width (fixed 115mm height, about half the page width) and the title block text is unreadable, overprinting itself (print-308_win.jpg, style.css:108,113).
Diameter dimensions (P1, P2, H1, H2, G1, E1) have no extension lines; only the lengths and R1 do.
Rule 8: on belted cases w also uses E + tb instead of the belt ramp end + tb (drawing.js:201-202).
Straight cases: the section bullet (G1) overlaps the wall, because tb runs up to the mouth (drawing.js:195), so the bullet is not shown cleanly inside the case.
Process artefacts: no README, specs, ADRs or CI delivered.
strengths: The drawing geometry is computed faithfully from the rules: chamfer, extractor groove, belt ramp at δ, rimfire half-round, rounded shoulder corners, a mathematically correct tangent ogive, heeled bullet, primer pocket and hatched section. Proportions match the reference drawings.
Data handling is correct and safe: values appear as published, tolerances inline, DMS angles, the brief's symbols, everything escaped, no network requests and no build step.
Meaningful automated tests: geometry checks, a label-overlap check over all 25 records, and jsdom tests of search, filter, routing and print.
issues: Print is broken: `.drawing text { font-size: inherit }` blows up the title block into overlapping, unreadable text, and the drawing prints at about half width instead of full width (print-308_win.jpg).

On screen the title block and drawing labels are badly scaled: labels are larger than the page heading, the title block is huge with a thick scaled border, and on short cartridges it dwarfs the drawing (detail-9_mm_luger.jpg, detail-22_long_rifle.jpg).
No README, docs, ADRs or CI, no pinned Node version, and a caret-range dev dependency. There are also geometry edge-case deviations: belted w, and the bullet overlapping the wall on straight cases.
review.verdict: The data layer, list and true-to-scale geometry are solid and well tested, and they meet most of the brief. A garbled printed title block, an oversized on-screen title block and label scale, and a repository with no documentation or CI mean it should not be published as is.
